use_when: Use it for one independent choice, such as keeping someone signed in.
Use Checked when the choice is on, and Unchecked when it is off.
Use Default for the resting empty box, and Hovered only while the pointer is over it.

dont_use_when.when: Do not use it when the choice takes effect immediately. Use a switch.
Do not use it for mutually exclusive options. Use a radio.
Do not detach the instance to recolor the border or the check.
Do not override the box size. It is fixed at 16 so rows of choices align.
Do not leave the label off. The box alone does not name the choice.

variant_intent.State=Default: Use Default for the resting empty box, and Hovered only while the pointer is over it.
variant_intent.State=Hovered: Use Default for the resting empty box, and Hovered only while the pointer is over it.
variant_intent.State=Checked: Use Checked when the choice is on, and Unchecked when it is off.
variant_intent.State=Unchecked: Use Checked when the choice is on, and Unchecked when it is off.
variant_intent.State=Disabled: Implement Disabled in code, not just visually. Color alone is not enough.

placement: Beside its label, between the last field and the form's Primary action: 'Email me deals and travel tips' sits between the Password field and 'Create Account' in the Figma 'Component Appearance' example.
The label sits beside the box, in sentence case (Figma Best Practice).

a11y.fact: Rendered as a native <button> with role="checkbox".
The accessible name comes from the label prop (aria-label); the box alone does not name the choice.
State=Disabled sets the real DOM disabled attribute.
Implement Disabled in code, not just visually. Color alone is not enough.
Keyboard focus is not in this set yet. Do not treat hover as a substitute.
